stories.title: BBOP Center Awards $10K to AI-Powered Sales Platform for Women
stories.summary: Kalilah Hudson won $10,000 in the BBOP Center's pitch competition for her AI-powered sales platform Clidelity, designed for women entrepreneurs. It's a win for inclusive innovation in the Inland Empire.
stories.extended_summary: Kalilah Hudson spent 14 years as a case manager helping thousands in foster care navigate complex systems. That experience inspired her to build Clidelity, an AI platform that guides women entrepreneurs through sales with a structured, relationship-based approach. At the Black and Brown Opportunities for Profit Center’s pitch competition, she walked away with nearly $10,000 in cash and support. The win validated her vision that innovation can thrive in San Bernardino. Clidelity is now poised to help more women grow their businesses.
stories.headline_split: BBOP Center Awards $10K to AI-Powered Sales Platform

stories.title: Simple tweaks can make wastewater treatment less polluting
stories.summary: Wastewater treatment plants can accidentally release nitrous oxide, a powerful greenhouse gas. But Cobalt Water Global uses machine learning to tweak the process—like aerating less—and cut emissions by up to 90%, turning a pollution problem into a climate win.
stories.extended_summary: Nitrous oxide, a potent global warming and ozone-depleting gas, is an unintended byproduct of wastewater treatment. But Jose Porro's company Cobalt Water Global has found that simple adjustments—like reducing aeration at certain times—can slash emissions by 80-90%. Using machine learning to monitor and fine-tune the microbes that break down nitrogen, utilities can clean water without adding to atmospheric pollution. It's a low-tech fix with huge potential for every treatment plant on the planet.
